question: A previously healthy 16-year-old boy comes to the physician because of a pruritic rash on the chest that has become progressively larger over the past 10 days. It is not painful. He is sexually active with two female partners and uses condoms inconsistently. He works part-time as a lifeguard. He has no family history of serious illness. He does not smoke. He drinks 5–6 beers on weekends. His temperature is 36.7°C (98°F), pulse is 66/min, and blood pressure is 110/70 mm Hg. A photograph of the rash is shown below. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Pruritic rash" -> "Progressively larger over 10 days" -> "Not painful" -> "Possible fungal infection" -> "Topical miconazole" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Pruritic rash" -> "Progressively larger over 10 days" -> "Not painful" -> "Possible contact dermatitis" -> "Topical hydrocortisone" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Pruritic rash" -> "Progressively larger over 10 days" -> "Not painful" -> "Possible pityriasis rosea" -> "Reassurance" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Pruritic rash" -> "Progressively larger over 10 days" -> "Not painful" -> "Possible bacterial infection" -> "Topical erythromycin" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Pruritic rash" -> "Progressively larger over 10 days" -> "Not painful" -> "Possible UV exposure related" -> "Phototherapy" -> 40%
analysis: The clinical presentation suggests a case of pityriasis rosea, which is characterized by a pruritic rash that often starts with a 'herald patch' followed by a more widespread rash. This condition is self-limiting and typically resolves on its own without specific treatment. The most appropriate management in this case is reassurance, as the condition is benign and self-limiting.
